flaw1_whitespace_split.description: REAL BUG. str.split(' ') keeps the empty string between consecutive spaces as a word; str.split() collapses whitespace runs. Ghost words inflate the denominator: eng 79 -> 78 (1 ghost), hin 62 -> 61 (1 ghost). DIRECTION: fertility is DEFLATED -- eng 1.2652 vs 1.2831 (-1.39%), hin 7.4485 vs 7.5985 (-1.97%).

flaw2_lowercasing.description: REAL BUG, but it biases AGAINST the v0 conclusion. Asymmetric transform: Hindi tokens are unchanged (459 -> 459, Devanagari has no case), while English tokens move 96 -> 99 (+3.1%) as GPT-2 BPE merge boundaries shift. DIRECTION: lowercasing RAISES the English token count, so it SHRINKS the reported disparity from 6.09x to 5.92x (-2.8%). The methodology is unsound because the transform is applied to only one side of the comparison -- but this particular bias understates the gap rather than inflating it, so correcting it makes v0's headline slightly WORSE, not better.

flaw3_macro_vs_micro.description: REAL STATISTICAL FLAW. fertility.py computes the macro-average sum(T_i/W_i)/N, which weights a 2-word line the same as a 50-word line; the corpus rate is the micro-average sum(T_i)/sum(W_i). DIRECTION: macro OVERSTATES both languages -- eng 1.2472 vs micro 1.2308 (+1.33%), hin 7.5985 vs micro 7.5246 (+0.98%). Small on this corpus, but it is the wrong estimator and its size is corpus-dependent.

flaw4_typology_words.description: REAL CONCEPTUAL FLAW. On the same 100 parallel sentences English uses 22.2 words/sent and Kannada 17.2 (22.6% fewer words for identical meaning), because Kannada binds case markers and postpositions onto the stem. Kannada therefore scores 17.07x English per WORD but only 13.22x per PARALLEL SENTENCE. DIRECTION: the word denominator INFLATES the apparent penalty by 29.1%, an artifact of morphology rather than tokenizer cost. The denominator must hold meaning constant across languages; whitespace words do not.

flaw5_codepoint_vs_bytes.description: REAL CONCEPTUAL FLAW. Python 3 len(str) counts Unicode CODE POINTS (PEP 393 flexible string representation) -- not UTF-8 bytes and not grapheme clusters. Indic aksharas span several code points (2.56 UTF-8 bytes per code point for Hindi vs 1.00 for English), so the denominator swells for Indic text while the numerator is untouched. MAGNITUDE: the identical tokens scored per code point give 7.21x, but scored per UTF-8 byte give 2.82x. DIRECTION: the code-point denominator OVERSTATES the disparity by 2.56x, and is the direct source of REPORT_v0's '7.0x worse per character' headline.

flaw6_shared_numerator_fallacy.description: REAL CONCEPTUAL FLAW in REPORT_v0's REASONING (not in the script). v0 argues the tok/char column 'confirms' the tok/word number and concludes 'no further measurement needed'. But both metrics divide the SAME numerator (token count T), and under gpt2 that numerator is dominated by a single artifact: Devanagari falling back to byte-level tokens. Changing only the DENOMINATOR cannot test that artifact, so agreement is arithmetically guaranteed rather than corroborative. Proof: swapping the denominator leaves both large (gpt2 6.15x per word, 7.21x per code point), but swapping the NUMERATOR collapses both at once (xlm-roberta-base 1.08x per word, 1.26x per code point). Independent confirmation requires a different tokenizer, not a different divisor.

harmless_nfc_normalization.description: HARMLESS AND NECESSARY. Hindi shows 0.00% because the 11 decomposable Devanagari code points Unicode defines (ऩऱऴक़ख़ग़...) do not occur in this corpus -- NFD(text)==text is True, so a Hindi-only test cannot show anything. Measured on Dravidian corpora, which do contain decomposable characters, dropping NFC inflates token counts: kan +4.52%, tam +1.47%, tel +0.65%. DIRECTION: removing NFC INFLATES tokens by up to 4.52%. NFC costs nothing and prevents that. Flagging it as a bug would be incorrect.

harmless_random_seed.description: HARMLESS -- dead code, not data sampling. Static scan of fertility.py finds 1 reference(s) to the random module (random.seed), of which 0 actually draw from the stream. Because nothing consumes the RNG, the seed cannot influence any reported number -- deleting line 25 changes every output by exactly 0. 'import sys' is likewise unused (0 call sites). Looks like hidden corpus sampling; is provably inert. Flagging it as a bug would be incorrect.

sample_size_variance.description: Sample-size caveat for A1: the 10-sentence smoke corpus gives 7.525 tok/word for Hindi, the 100-sentence parallel corpus gives 7.744 (+2.9%). The v0 headline rests on the noisier of the two.
